title: Transparent Trace Adapter with Rewriting, Hold-and-Replay, and Downstream Graceful Degradation
creator: Alexandra Kim
description: Build a transparent trace-adapter service that accepts OpenTelemetry/OTLP spans and ensures reliable delivery to downstream backends (Tempo/Jaeger vendors) via schema-tolerant rewriting, idempotent buffering with TTL hold-and-replay, and tenant-aware routing. The adapter must perform non-destructive span normalization (timestamp correction, trace-id v1/v2 compatibility, default service.name mapping), add lightweight provenance headers, and expose health/lag metrics and debug endpoints so Console can visualize delayed deliveries and SLO impact.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts OTLP gRPC and HTTP JSON ingest and returns 202 on valid payloads
When downstream is healthy, spans are routed with <200ms median extra latency compared to direct ingest in perf harness
When downstream is unavailable, spans are buffered per-tenant up to configured TTL (default 2h) and retried with exponential backoff; no data loss observed in integration test with Tempo mock
Span rewriting preserves original attributes and adds a single 'rw.provenance' attribute; no fields are removed unless explicitly redacted by tenant policy
Deduplication key prevents double-import when replay overlaps with live-forwarding (idempotency proven in end-to-end test)
Adapter exposes Prometheus metrics: buffered_spans_per_tenant, replay_rate, last_success_timestamp_{backend}, rewrite_error_rate; Console dashboard updated
Runbook created for buffer saturation, replay storms, and downstream credential rotation scenarios
comments: 2026-02-25 - Alexandra Kim: Initial ticket created. Problem: multiple tenants observed span loss during transient Tempo outages. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/transparent-trace-adapter-draft

2026-02-27 - Marcus Chen: Spike completed against a Tempo mock. Discovered that some legacy Jaeger clients send trace IDs in UUID v1 format which Tempo accepts but our current hashing caused inconsistent sharding. Change: normalize trace ID form for shard key while storing original trace_id in metadata.

2026-03-01 - Marcus Chen: Prototype implemented buffering layer using bounded priority queue per-tenant with disk-backed overflow (S3). Local perf: forwarding adds ~120ms median; replay throughput cap validated at 20k spans/s on c5.4xlarge. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/4122

2026-03-03 - Design review (Leah Ortiz): Approved non-destructive rewrite approach; flagged UI requirement to surface replayed vs live-ingested spans. Action: add 'rw.replayed' boolean attribute on replayed spans and update Console schema.

2026-03-05 - Security review kickoff (Priya Sharma): Buffering persisted to S3 must be encrypted with customer KMS when tenant has KMS flag; added gate to encryption flow. Pending security review item: HSM key rotation impact on replay credentials.

2026-03-07 - Marcus Chen: Integration tests against Tempo mock show dedupe key collision when spans split across 64k batch boundary. Mitigation: use composite key (trace_id + span_id + original_ingest_timestamp_ms) for idempotency. Updating unit tests.

2026-03-09 - QA (Rafael Gomez): Running chaos test simulating Tempo outage with staggered recovery. Observed replay storm risk when many tenants recover simultaneously. Plan: implement staggered replay window and jittered backoff per-tenant; add circuit-breaker to fail fast for backends with repeated 5xx.

2026-03-10 - Marcus Chen: Implemented jitter/backoff and added extra metrics for Console. Preparing canary rollout: dedicated canary pool (2 nodes) routing only internal-test tenant flags. Playbook for rollback created: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/trace-adapter-replay-rollback
notes: Operational concerns: need alert for 'buffered_spans_total' > 80% of capacity for three consecutive minutes
Rollout plan: canary -> 10% tenants -> 50% -> global over two weeks with automated health checks and slow-start replay
Follow-ups: tenant-level retention policy UI in Console, per-tenant KMS binding support, and a diagnostic endpoint to stream buffered spans for debugging
